arabic text: Saamne darbar ke ghairate Sajjad ka hai yeh kaisa imtehaan\nTeen deen guzre khari hai, fatema ki betiyan
english translation text: Before the court, what a trial this is for Sajjad’s honour.\nFor three days, Fatema’s daughters have stood waiting.

arabic text: Sham wale has rahe hai bekaso ko dekh kar\nHai charagha chaarsu aur saj rahe hai bamodar\nBabe saat par ruka hai bekason ka karvan
english translation text: The people of Shaam laugh upon seeing the helpless captives.\nLights blaze on every side and the rooftops are decorated.\nAt Bab al-Sa‘at, the caravan of the defenceless has been halted.

arabic text: Khoon rota hai jo aabid usko ye ehsaas hai\nHaiii fatema Zahra ki chaadar shamiyo ke paas hai\nDekh kar kehti hai zainab mere ghazi ho kahaan
english translation text: Abid weeps blood because he knows\nthat Fatema Zahra’s veil is in the hands of the Syrians.\nSeeing this, Zainab cries, “My Ghazi, where are you?”

arabic text: Sar ali akbar ka neze par utha te hain shaqi\nSunchuki satra azaane be rida binte alia\nRo rahi hai har azaan sun kar ali akbar ki maa
english translation text: The cruel ones raise Ali Akbar’s head upon the spear.\nAli’s unveiled daughter has already heard seventeen calls to prayer.\nAt every azaan, Ali Akbar’s mother weeps.

arabic text: Misle Zahra sar jhukaye shamiyon me aagayi\nHaii chaar bhai some sakina par zaifi chagayi\nKaan bhi zakhmi hai gaalon par tamachon ke nishan
english translation text: Like Zahra, she entered Shaam with her head bowed.\nThough only four years old, Sakina has been aged by grief.\nHer ears are wounded and her cheeks bear the marks of slaps.

arabic text: Khoon ke aansoo tapakte hai sar shabir se\nPuchti hai jab sakina zainabe dilgeer se\nAi phupi amma yahaa se kab chalega karwan
english translation text: Tears of blood fall from Shabbir’s severed head\nwhen Sakina asks the grief-stricken Zainab:\n“Aunt, when will this caravan leave this place?”

arabic text: Sab se mushkil marhala sajjad pe yawar ye tha\nHai sham ke darbar mein jab qaafela jaane laga\nParh rahi thi inna lillah us ghari sab bibiyan
english translation text: Yawar, the hardest stage for Sajjad was this:\nwhen the caravan was about to enter the court of Shaam,\nevery lady recited, “Indeed, we belong to Allah …”
